title: Role alignment day-zero prep and mentor script
content:
Purpose:
A compact, pragmatic playbook to get hiring managers, hiring panelists, and assigned mentors aligned before an accepted offer lands and through day 0 -> day 30. Focus: reduce first-week ambiguity, shorten time-to-impact, and make hiring decisions consistent across roles.

Scope and intended audience:
- People Ops partner, hiring manager, interviewer panel, assigned mentor/peer buddy.
- Applies to full-time ICs and senior IC hires (individual contributor engineering and product roles).
- Lightweight variant of the 90d onboarding framework for small teams or fast hires.

Quick preboarding (before offer accepted / once accepted but before first day):
- Hiring manager: send welcome note with team org chart, first-day agenda, primary Slack channel and access instructions. (Template: CONF-people-onboarding-2025)
- People Ops: create IT ticket, hardware request, calendar invites for 1:1s for the first 30 days, badge access if on-site.
- Mentor: schedule 30/60/90 checkpoint meetings and block 1 hour/day for first 3 days for pairing.
- Candidate: short reading list (team docs, product one-pager, top 3 codebases to skim).
- Admin: share first-week list (account creation steps) and a short checklist to complete before end of day 2.

Day-zero / Day-one role-alignment checklist for hiring manager (scripted items to run through):
1) Role intent summary (60–90s): why we hired this role, top 2 goals for the first 90 days, and how success will be measured.
2) Team context (2–3 mins): current roadmap slice, immediate teammates, known constraints.
3) Quick org map (1 min): who to loop in for product, infra, QA, design.
4) Early wins (2 mins): 2 small, high-signal tasks the hire can complete in week 1 to build momentum.
5) Signals we care about (2 mins): shipping frequency, test coverage baseline, peer feedback cadence.
6) Logistics (2 mins): regular 1:1 cadence, expectations for async updates, code review SLAs.
7) Open questions (1–2 mins): invite the new hire to surface any immediate blockers and preferences.

Mentor / buddy script (use as a loose transcript for the first 60 minutes pairing):
- Intro + context (5 mins): name, role, what you do day-to-day, your suggestion for first 48hrs.
- Environment walkthrough (10 mins): local dev setup gotchas, common flakiness, test command cheat sheet.
- First hands-on task (30–40 mins): pair on a smoke-change that exercises the deploy/test path; mentor drives until the hire is comfortable.
- Closeout (5 mins): recap, link to follow-ups, schedule next pairing slot.

Interviewer panel: lightweight rubric for consistent hiring signals
- Use a 1–5 scale. Each band maps to observable behaviors. Score each section separately and add notes.

Technical competence (1–5):
1: Unable to reason about basic abstractions for role (e.g., cannot decompose problem).
3: Solves standard problems with some gaps; needs scaffolding but delivers working design.
5: Clear design tradeoffs, anticipates edge cases, balances correctness vs. speed.

Collaborative craft (1–5):
1: Troubles with peer communication and feedback; defensive posture.
3: Gives and receives feedback; works through disagreements.
5: Elevates discussions, clarifies ambiguity, mentors others in-session.

Delivery and ownership (1–5):
1: No evidence of end-to-end delivery.
3: Owns discrete milestones; cross-functional handoffs usually complete.
5: Drives complex initiatives, negotiates scope, consistently delivers measurable outcomes.

Cultural fit / values alignment (1–5):
1: Repeatedly misaligned with core values or operating norms.
3: Generally aligned; articulates tradeoffs consistent with our principles.
5: Exemplifies behaviors and helps raise the bar for the team.

Redwood-specific safety signals to call out in notes:
- Unclear short-term ramp plan from the candidate side.
- Repeated inability to explain tradeoffs when timeboxed.
- Consistently low curiosity on product context.

Decision guidance for hiring manager (post-interview synthesis):
- Hire: at least three categories scored 4+ and no 1s; interview notes include concrete examples of past impact.
- Hire with reservations: one 3 and rest 4+ OR strong functional skill with weaker cross-functional signals but a clear ramp plan.
- No hire: any 1 in core competency or repeated red flags across multiple interviews.

Selection matrix (quick tie-breaker heuristics):
- Prefer candidate with explicit prior ownership of a shipped feature that matches our scale.
- Prefer paired-coding outcomes that completed the end-to-end path (not just whiteboard thoughts).
- If multiple acceptable candidates, bias to cross-team communicators who have product-context experience.

First 30-day activation checklist (mentor + manager split):
Manager (what to assign/measure):
- Week 1: first incremental deploy or documented test run (measure: completed PR + checklist).
- Week 2: two cross-team introductions and an outlined 30-day project plan.
- Week 3–4: initial stakeholder demo and written retrospective on ramp blockers.

Mentor:
- Daily short pairing for first 3 days, then 3x/week through week 2.
- Shadowing on one support rotation.
- Review and comment on first PRs within 24 hours.

Example early-win task ideas (role-agnostic):
- Fix a flaky test and add a regression case.
- Update a small doc (README or runbook) with missing steps.
- Implement a visibility metric in an existing dashboard for a team KPI.

Handoff checklist to close onboarding sprint at 30 days:
- New hire has green build and deployed small change in main branch.
- Mentor sign-off on local dev hygiene and testing familiarity.
- Manager and hire aligned on 60-day goal with clear success criteria.
- Ticket with retrospective notes created (JIRA tag HIRE-xxxx-ramp).

Common traps and mitigation notes (people-ops):
- Trap: Overloading first week with meetings.
  Mitigation: Keep day 1 heavy on pairing and light on long meetings; defer 1-hour cross-functional reviews until week 2.
- Trap: Too many parallel access requests (blocks development).
  Mitigation: Pre-create accounts where possible and verify access on day 0.
- Trap: Mentor burnout when multiple new hires land the same week.
  Mitigation: Rotate mentors; create short recorded walkthroughs to scale availability.

Notes to people ops when closing the role:
- Capture example PRs and initial metrics that signaled success (to reuse in future role briefs).
- If hire had an incremental ramp plan, save as a template under CONF-people-onboarding-2025/templates.

Appendix: sample interview note template (copy into Panel Google doc)
- Candidate name:
- Role applied:
- Interviewer:
- Date:
- Scores: Technical / Collaborative / Delivery / Culture (numbers)
- Top evidence bullets (3):
  1) Past shipped example + measurable impact.
  2) Observable behavior in interview (paired task outcome, communication).
  3) Risk/unknowns and mitigation plan.
- Recommendation: Hire / Hire with reservations / No hire

End of doc — quick TODOs for reviewer: add links for first-week reading list, update manager templates for exec-level hires, and confirm mentor rotation calendar for Q1 2026.

Notes to self: rough draft; intended to be easy to print and hand to mentors as a 1-pager. Contains some overlap with existing onboarding playbooks but intentionally condensed and scripted for time-boxed first-day interactions.
